expectations.text: Cites at least 8 distinct real Generative AI Lens best-practice IDs (GENOPS/GENSEC/GENREL/GENPERF/GENCOST/GENSUS nn-BPnn)
expectations.evidence: Programmatic scan of outputs/review.md for the pattern GEN[A-Z]+nn-BPnn returned zero matches. The review uses its own invented identifier scheme instead — SEC-1..SEC-18, REL-1..REL-11, PERF-1..PERF-9, COST-1..COST-9, OPS-1..OPS-10, SUS-1..SUS-4, RAI-1..RAI-8. Section 4.7 is even titled 'Responsible AI (GenAI Lens)' and the header claims 'Reviewed against: AWS Well-Architected Framework (six pillars) + Generative AI Lens', but no Lens best-practice ID appears anywhere.

expectations.text: Every GEN*-BP* ID cited actually exists in the Lens — no fabricated IDs
expectations.evidence: Zero GEN*-BP* IDs were cited (verified by script against assets/best-practices.csv), so nothing was fabricated. Passing vacuously: the run invented no Lens IDs, though it also cited none. Note the locally-invented SEC-/REL-/OPS- identifiers are clearly presented as the document's own numbering, not as Lens IDs, so they are not fabrications.

expectations.text: Flags the wildcard IAM policy (bedrock:* and Resource="*" in infra/main.tf) as a least-privilege gap tied to GENSEC01-BP01 or GENSEC01-BP03
expectations.evidence: The gap is found and located precisely — 'SEC-5 | H | IAM: `bedrock:*` on `Resource = "*"` — permits DeleteKnowledgeBase, model customization, provisioned throughput purchases, not just inference | main.tf:110-113' and SEC-6 for the s3 wildcard — but it is not tied to GENSEC01-BP01 or GENSEC01-BP03, which appear nowhere in the document. The substantive finding is present; the required Lens mapping is absent.

expectations.text: Identifies that no Bedrock Guardrail is configured and maps it to GENSEC02-BP01
expectations.evidence: The absence is identified twice — 'SEC-9 | H | No Bedrock Guardrail — no PII filtering, no denied topics, no jailbreak detection, no grounding check | absent' and 'RAI-3 | H | No guardrails of any kind' — but GENSEC02-BP01 is never named, so the required mapping is missing.

expectations.text: Identifies the hardcoded API key literal in src/handler.py
expectations.evidence: §2.2: '`src/handler.py:16` hardcodes `API_KEY = "sk-acme-support-2f8a91"` — checked into git, baked into the deployment zip, shared across all callers, never rotated.' Also SEC-3 and remediation item 4 ('Rotate the API key'). Exact literal and line number verified against the fixture.

expectations.text: Connects the README's 'confidently wrong 1 in 20' complaint to the absence of a ground-truth evaluation set (GENPERF01-BP01 or GENOPS01-BP01)
expectations.evidence: The substantive connection is made well: 'OPS-2 | H | **No evaluation harness.** "Confidently wrong 1 in 20 but we can't measure it" is a tooling gap, not a mystery. Needs a golden question set with expected answers, offline scoring on faithfulness/groundedness/context-precision run in CI...'. However, neither GENPERF01-BP01 nor GENOPS01-BP01 is cited. Graded against the same standard applied throughout this eval — an assertion that names specific Lens IDs requires those IDs to appear — so this fails on the mapping only, not on the analysis.

expectations.text: Addresses the cross-customer data exposure incident — one knowledge base holding all customers' account records with no per-customer access filtering
expectations.evidence: §2.1 'There is no tenant isolation in retrieval — CRITICAL': 'retrieve() (src/handler.py:28-36) issues a pure semantic search across the entire index with numberOfResults: 20 and no filter clause ... the billing team's ETL writes account records ... into the same S3 bucket as the public help-centre articles. Public marketing content and confidential per-customer PII share one bucket, one knowledge base, one vector index, and one retrieval path.' It also correctly reframes the README incident: 'was not an anomaly — it is the designed behaviour of this system, and it will recur', and routes it to privacy/legal for breach assessment.

expectations.text: Attributes the 429s and latency spikes to throughput management, citing GENREL01-BP01 or GENOPS02-BP03
expectations.evidence: The attribution is correct and detailed — root-cause table row: 'Occasional 429s from Bedrock | No retry config with adaptive/jittered backoff; no cross-region inference profile; no provisioned throughput; single region (us-east-1 is the most contended) | REL-1, REL-2' — but neither GENREL01-BP01 nor GENOPS02-BP03 is cited anywhere in the document.

expectations.text: Attributes the tripled Bedrock bill to specific cost practices (20-result retrieval, max_tokens 4096, no prompt caching) with a GENCOST ID
expectations.evidence: All three specific drivers are named in the §2.4 driver table — 'Over-retrieval | numberOfResults: 20 (handler.py:33)', 'Oversized generations | max_tokens: 4096 ... (handler.py:19,53,54)', 'No caching | No cache layer anywhere' (plus PERF-4 'No Bedrock prompt caching for the static system-prompt prefix') — but no GENCOST ID accompanies them. The assertion explicitly requires 'with a GENCOST ID'.

expectations.text: Includes a per-practice status table using Met / Partially met / Not met / Not applicable
expectations.evidence: No per-practice status table exists. The document's tables are severity-graded finding lists (columns: ID | Sev | Finding | Location, with values Critical/High/Medium/Low) and a pillar-level 'readiness at a glance' table using free-text ratings ('Critical risk', 'High risk', 'Medium risk'). Nothing enumerates Lens practices, and no Met / Partially met / Not met / Not applicable vocabulary appears anywhere.

expectations.text: Every priority finding cites concrete evidence — a file, Terraform resource, or README statement — rather than generic advice
expectations.evidence: All five items in §2 'The five things you will get hammered on' anchor to specific code: §2.1 'src/handler.py:39-46 ... src/handler.py:28-36'; §2.2 'src/handler.py:16 ... infra/main.tf:75 ... the widget is embedded on the public support site'; §2.3 'src/handler.py:21 ... src/handler.py:54 "temperature": 0.9'; §2.4 'numberOfResults: 20 (handler.py:33)'; §2.5 'infra/main.tf:55 sets timeout = 300'. Verified against the fixture — handler.py:16/21/33/54 and main.tf:55/75/110-113/140-143 all resolve to the claimed content.

expectations.text: States the review scope (which pillars were assessed) explicitly
expectations.evidence: Header: '**Scope reviewed:** infra/main.tf, src/handler.py, README.md' and '**Reviewed against:** AWS Well-Architected Framework (six pillars) + Generative AI Lens'. The 'Pillar readiness at a glance' table then names each pillar assessed — Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence, Sustainability, Responsible AI (GenAI Lens) — and §4 is organised into one subsection per pillar.

claims.claim: The document was 'Reviewed against: AWS Well-Architected Framework (six pillars) + Generative AI Lens'
claims.evidence: Not substantiated. The document never cites a single Generative AI Lens best practice, question, or design principle by identifier or name. §4.7 is labelled 'Responsible AI (GenAI Lens)' but its contents (RAI-1..RAI-8) are the author's own framing, not Lens material. The claim of reviewing against the Lens is unverifiable from the output.

claims.claim: 'Findings by severity: 6 Critical · 11 High · 14 Medium · 8 Low' (39 findings)
claims.evidence: Counted across §4.1-§4.7: Critical = SEC-1,2,3,4 + RAI-1,2 = 6. High = SEC-5..SEC-10 (6) + REL-1..REL-4 (4) + PERF-1,2 (2) + COST-1..COST-4 (4) + OPS-1,2,3 (3) + RAI-3,4 (2) = 21, not 11. Medium and Low likewise do not reconcile. The headline severity tally is wrong; total findings across the tables is 69, not 39. No assertion catches this.

claims.claim: AOSS 'bills a minimum OCU floor 24/7 regardless of traffic — frequently the surprise line item at this scale'
claims.evidence: Accurate for OpenSearch Serverless, and a genuinely useful observation the with_skill run did not make: the README says 'Bedrock spend has roughly tripled' but the AOSS floor is a non-Bedrock line item that may explain part of the confusion about 'the shape of the bill'.

claims.claim: The deployed stack cannot match the repo — aws_lambda_permission, aws_bedrockagent_data_source, AOSS policies and the vector index are all missing from Terraform
claims.evidence: Checked infra/main.tf — none of these resources are declared, and the AOSS encryption-policy point is correct (collections cannot be created without one). §5 is a substantive finding that no assertion covers.

suggestions.reason: This baseline is technically excellent — it found every planted defect (tenant isolation, hardcoded key, wildcard IAM, temperature 0.9, timeout mismatch, missing guardrail, no eval harness) plus several the with_skill run missed (the AOSS OCU cost floor, the missing aws_lambda_permission, timing-unsafe key comparison, no conversation history). Seven of its failures are purely 'did not cite the Lens ID'. If the eval is meant to measure Lens grounding specifically, that is the correct result; but the assertion set currently gives no signal on analytical quality independent of ID citation, so a run that cited IDs while analysing badly would score higher than this one. Consider splitting the ID-mapping assertions into a substance half and a citation half.

suggestions.assertion: Connects the README's 'confidently wrong 1 in 20' complaint to the absence of a ground-truth evaluation set (GENPERF01-BP01 or GENOPS01-BP01)
suggestions.reason: The parenthetical is ambiguous — it reads either as an acceptance criterion (must cite one of these IDs) or as a gloss identifying which practice is meant. I graded it as a criterion for consistency with the neighbouring 'tied to' / 'citing' / 'with a GENCOST ID' assertions, but the wording should be made explicit so the verdict does not hinge on the grader's reading.

No assertion checks internal consistency of the output's own numbers. This run's headline 'Findings by severity: 6 Critical · 11 High · 14 Medium · 8 Low' does not reconcile with its own finding tables (21 High, 69 findings total). A cheap, discriminating assertion would be 'any summary counts reconcile with the detailed findings'.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertions cleanly separate Lens-grounded review from generic architecture review, which is the point — but they under-measure analysis quality, so this run's score understates how good the document is.
